source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for End-to-End Self-Driving
source.authors: Manav Gagvani; Benjamin Namikas; Sivamurugan Velmurugan; N. Kumar; Shreyyash Sharma; Thomas Peterson; Pratyush Mathur; Hyunseo Chang; R. Paleja

record.tranche_reason: The study measures SAE feature organization in a driving planner, but does not test dictionary-size splitting, parent–child input coverage, or geometric relations between features at different SAE sizes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE co-activation clusters, their alignment with route intent and speed, and clustering robustness. These are related findings about SAE representations, but do not measure the size-dependent splitting described in the claim. It trains 384-latent SAEs; it does not compare dictionary sizes or match features across SAEs.
record.test_reason: The study trains one 384-latent TopK SAE per block of a driving planner and analyses co-activation clusters, visual edits and steering. It never varies dictionary size, matches features across SAEs, tests parent–child absorption, or compares training objectives, so its results bear on no version of feature splitting.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: SAE latents in SMTS are structured, visually grounded and steerable, and an SAE-latent scoring adapter reduces ADE@5s by 3.44%. The paper draws no conclusion about feature splitting.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains TopK SAEs with an AuxK loss on driving-planner query activations; it does not reproduce or compare the original feature-splitting method.
record.method_sensitivity: Co-activation cluster structure varies with the correlation threshold: threshold 0.20 collapses many features into one component, while thresholds 0.35 and 0.40 yield multiple clusters.

fits_no_version.finding: Co-activation clusters of block-3 SAE latents align with route intent (98.3% accuracy), and two straight clusters split by speed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents in an end-to-end driving planner form co-activation groups aligned with route intent and speed.

fits_no_version.finding: Cluster structure depends on the correlation threshold but is largely preserved by modularity clustering (94.3% agreement).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The co-activation grouping of this SAE is threshold-sensitive but robust to the choice of clustering algorithm.

record.problems: For the claim at issue, the study evaluates only one stated SAE latent dimension and reports no cross-size feature matching, input partition test, or geometric comparison of candidate parent and child features.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results directly test feature splitting across dictionary sizes. Other SAE analyses, including counterfactual edits and steering, do not measure the claim's parent–child splitting pattern.

untested.parts: No large language models or open SAE releases; one small driving planner.
No nested families across sizes or decoder-geometry analysis of split features.
No parent/child absorption test or size/sparsity sweep.
No cross-size latent decomposition or novel-latent analysis.
No comparison of SAE objectives (e.g. Matryoshka).

record.verdict_notes: The threshold sweep (R4, R5) can look like splitting, since one component becomes four, then six. It reflects graph-construction granularity within a fixed SAE, not dictionary growth, so it should not be linked to V1 or V3. The record's relation and tranche (discusses/T6) are kept; 'cites_only' would also be defensible, since the paper does not discuss splitting at all.

versions.untested_parts: No SAE dictionary-size comparison or test of whether finer features partition a smaller feature's inputs or lie near its direction.
No testing across model scales or open SAE releases; the study analyzes one driving model.
No test of nested feature families, parent–child relations, or geometric closeness between split features.
No parent/child latent comparison or test of feature absorption across SAE sizes or sparsity settings.
No comparison of larger- and smaller-SAE latents, combinations of latents across dictionaries, or novel latents across sizes.
No comparison of SAE objectives or test of whether an objective causes splitting.

rows.subject: SMTS
rows.operation_detail: Grouped binarized SAE activations using pairwise Pearson correlation at threshold 0.35.
rows.measure: Number and sizes of co-activation clusters
rows.note: This reports co-activation groups within one SAE, not feature splitting across dictionary sizes.
rows.check: Co-activation clusters within a single SAE; no cross-size comparison.

rows.subject: SMTS
rows.operation_detail: Assigned scenes to the cluster with the highest mean activation and mapped clusters to route intents by majority vote.
rows.measure: Route-intent classification accuracy from cluster assignment
rows.value: 98.3% overall; 99.8% straight, 92.9% left turns, and 86.4% right turns
rows.note: Intent alignment does not test size-dependent splitting.
rows.check: Intent recovery from clusters; unrelated to splitting.

rows.subject: SMTS
rows.operation_detail: Summarized speed among the 50 scenes with highest activation for each cluster.
rows.value: C0: −1.04 standard deviations; C2: +0.98 standard deviations
rows.note: The two clusters share straight-driving intent and differ in speed; the study does not establish a parent–child feature relation.
rows.check: Speed separation of two straight clusters within one SAE; not a parent–child or size-dependent relation.

rows.subject: SMTS
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the co-activation clustering with correlation threshold 0.20.
rows.value: One component containing 238 features; described as combining distinct driving modes
rows.note: Threshold sensitivity concerns co-activation clustering, not SAE dictionary-size splitting.
rows.check: Varies the clustering threshold, not dictionary size. The analysis choice is the coarser or finer grouping, not the SAE.

rows.subject: SMTS
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the co-activation clustering with correlation threshold 0.40.
rows.measure: Cluster count and retention of primary-cluster features
rows.baseline: Threshold 0.35: four clusters of 64, 36, 34, and 27 features
rows.value: Six clusters; the four principal clusters retain 43/64, 27/36, 29/34, and 23/27 features, and two additional components have three features each
rows.note: The study says dominant intents remain unchanged; this threshold sweep does not test splitting across SAE sizes.
rows.check: Same as R4. The 'additional clusters' at τ=0.40 come from the graph threshold, not from feature splitting.

rows.subject: SMTS
rows.operation_detail: Compared connected-component clusters with greedy modularity maximization.

conditions.value: greedy modularity versus connected components at threshold 0.35

rows.measure: Fraction of retained features assigned the same matched cluster label
rows.note: Agreement between clustering procedures is not a test of geometric proximity or size-dependent splitting.
rows.check: Agreement between clustering methods; a robustness check of the study's own procedure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
